title: A rehearsal in light
summary: Give a producer one half-open stage curtain and three cues. The folded fabric and its hem reveal exactly what each light does.

layout.skeleton: Give the viewing frame one half-open curtain on a stage. Put three named cue choices and the selected technique together 16 px below the frame. Keep the brand in a compact title line.
layout.focus: One curtain, three broad folds and one turned hem make the light direction visible. The same folds and floor stay fixed in every cue.
layout.desktop: Compose a 960 × 420 stage centered in a 960 px column. Center a compact controls block directly below. Fit frame, choices and technique in the 900 px viewport.
layout.mobile: Use 16 px side margins and a 358 × 300 scene. Keep the lit hem, choice row and matching technique visible together in the initial 390 × 844 view.
layout.rhythm: Separate the three choices by at least 8 px. Keep the current technique close below them. Let the full-width stage and its folds carry the composition.

imagery.subject: Draw a half-open slate #626B74 stage curtain with three broad folds and a turned hem. Amber #E8A348 washes the folds, hard white side light catches one edge and casts a sharp floor shadow, and blue light from behind reveals the gap.
imagery.crop: Keep both the high folds and the lit hem inside the frame at both widths. Draw the broad folds without procedural grain.
imagery.fallback: Use three original stills of the same cloth and stage. Supply a short technique label and an accessible description of the illuminated folds.

motion.effect: Switch light, readable technique and the selected marker immediately. Fade a small selection marker alone.
motion.reduced: Change the lighting and every state together without motion.

action.instruction: Use native controls labeled Choose a cue. Keep a persistent filled selection and a separate inset focus outline. Let the keyboard choose every cue and make the matching technique and description update immediately.
action.label: Use the actual cue name

why: A curtain familiar to a theatre producer turns the action into a practical demonstration of wash, side light and backlight.

sources.observation: Driving the car demonstrates the creative developer's work while the visitor explores the portfolio. The site lists a map, respawn and multiple input methods.
The studio offers standard Work and Connect navigation alongside an optional themed command interface.

credit: Original stage composition inspired by Bruno Simon and ToyFight. Use only original artwork.

title: The river changes the town
summary: Build the story along one measurable cross-section. A selectable elevation changes the illustrated bank and the list of affected places.

layout.skeleton: Use a clean three-step bank section. Give each physically distinct crossing a large original silhouette and put its short HTML name on a separate label rail aligned to that step.
layout.focus: A bold teal waterline climbs the three visible bank steps. Show the visual moment it reaches the path, ferry or bridge along with the cumulative readable result.
layout.desktop: Use a compact header and keep the selector and complete answer adjacent to the bank section. Keep the primary graphic within 440 px of height.
layout.mobile: Place the level selector and full closure result first. Follow with a 250–300 px stepped chart. Reserve at least 100 px of separate label rail and keep the place names at 16 px or larger.
layout.rhythm: Use the three equal threshold heights to form confident graphic steps and leave visible space between large crossing shapes and their label rail.

imagery.subject: Draw a sloping walking path, broad ferry at its dock, and tall bridge span as three large authored shapes. Use teal #61BCD4 for the water and gold #F2C35E beside labeled closures. Use clear solid colors and no small topographic textures.
imagery.crop: Keep all three silhouettes and their aligned, separate HTML names visible at 390 px. Retain the bold waterline and units.
imagery.fallback: Keep the three contour lines, their readable place names and the live closure list. Simplify the drawing before reducing text size.

motion.effect: Snap the waterline and closure labels to the selected level together. Give only the new level marker one brief emphasis.
motion.reduced: Use the immediate new level and matching list without the marker animation.

action.instruction: Use three named level controls with a visible persistent selected state. Update the current level, waterline and cumulative text outcome together. Preserve all supplied facts and the visible keyboard focus.
action.label: Use each supplied level and its units

why: The water line makes the relationship between height and closures visible. The text and controls still let a visitor answer the question quickly.

sources.observation: The ascent orders the exhibits by real altitude. The Kármán line is one of the named markers.
Depth provides the organizing scale of an explorable ocean story.

credit: Original river cross-section inspired by Neal Agarwal's single-axis stories.
